reader.summary: 15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer with some AI background would follow most of the lesson, but would get stuck where the three kinds of AI are treated as separate boxes, and where Step 2 points to an outline they do not have.

history.summary: 15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer with some AI background would follow most of the lesson, but would get stuck where the three kinds of AI are treated as separate boxes, and where Step 2 points to an outline they do not have.

18-more-question-practice.html 8/10. A newcomer with the earlier lessons would mostly follow this practice set, but would stumble on the pointers back to lessons: “Key terms” is a topic, not a lesson, and the intro says nine questions when there are ten.
15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer would get most stuck on the governance step, where the lesson points to an official outline and an exam it never names or explains.

15-ai-in-service-management.html 8/10. A newcomer would most struggle with an agent that acts on its own, since the lesson says a person checks real-consequence actions but never explains how an autonomous action is kept under human oversight, and with a pointer to an outline it never names.

15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer would follow the steps but get stuck on a reference to a document they cannot open, a sorting-game category the lesson never introduces, and one unclear sentence about what counts as a good enough error rate.

10-incidents-and-problems.html 9/10, 12-service-desk-and-requests.html 8/10. A newcomer would struggle most with how the two ideas work together in practice: how priority is worked out from impact and urgency in the incidents lesson, and what a configuration record is for beyond one example in the service desk lesson.

10-incidents-and-problems.html 8/10, 12-service-desk-and-requests.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the configuration idea: the lesson treats 'configuration management' and 'configuration record' as if they were the same thing, and Step 4 crowds several new ideas into one paragraph.
10-incidents-and-problems.html 9/10, 12-service-desk-and-requests.html 8/10.

10-incidents-and-problems.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly trip on ITSM words used before they are explained, such as service desk and root cause, and on the 9:00 ranking example, where the rule that decides the order is never stated outright.

03-grammar-in-use.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on small wording gaps, such as an unclear sorting prompt, a term (exception) used without a definition and a question pattern that appears in a code box and is never explained.

06-measuring-progress-honestly.html 8/10, 03-grammar-in-use.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with layout and notation in the grammar lesson: a pattern box sits under the wrong step, and a plus sign means two different things, while the measuring lesson's range step packs too many numbers into one paragraph.

05-boards-and-daily-habits.html 8/10, 06-measuring-progress-honestly.html 8/10, 03-grammar-in-use.html 8/10. A newcomer would most struggle with an unclear pattern or term used before it is shown, such as a question pattern named without an example, and in the agile lessons with 'cycle' and 'iteration' used for the same thing.
